intro.heading: Roofing Built for Houston's Climate
intro.body_p1: Houston subjects residential roofs to a demanding combination of climate stressors: roughly 50 inches of annual rainfall, direct exposure to Atlantic hurricane and tropical storm systems that can deliver sustained winds well above design thresholds for standard asphalt shingles, and intense summer heat that drives roof surface temperatures significantly above ambient air temperature. Between storm seasons, persistent UV exposure and high humidity continue to degrade shingles, flashing sealants, and underlayment. The cumulative effect of these conditions accelerates wear on every roofing component — making professional inspection a practical priority for Houston homeowners, not an optional formality.
intro.body_p2: Home Team serves homeowners and commercial property owners across the Greater Houston area with the same approach: a thorough, no-pressure inspection, followed by honest options and clear pricing. We work from our base in Tomball, keeping us well-positioned to serve northwest Houston, Harris County, and the surrounding communities. Whether you are dealing with storm damage, a recurring leak, or a roof approaching the end of its useful life — and whether or not an insurance claim is involved — we walk you through the full picture clearly so you can make a confident decision.

items.q: How does Houston's hurricane exposure affect residential roofing?
items.a: Houston sits in one of the most hurricane-active coastal corridors in the United States. Even storms that make landfall south of the city can deliver sustained winds of 50–80 mph and higher gusts to the Houston metro area. Standard three-tab asphalt shingles are typically rated for winds up to 60–70 mph; architectural shingles with enhanced wind resistance can be rated considerably higher. After any named storm or significant wind event, a professional inspection is warranted — shingles can sustain structural damage that is not visible from the ground but significantly shortens the roof's remaining lifespan. Home Team offers free post-storm inspections throughout Greater Houston.

items.q: Houston gets around 50 inches of rain a year — what does that mean for my roof?
items.a: Fifty inches of annual rainfall means every potential vulnerability in your roofing system gets tested repeatedly. Flashing seals at chimneys, vents, skylights, and any roof penetration are exposed to driving rain multiple times per year, and any gap in a sealant allows water to enter slowly but consistently. Gutters and downspouts sized for drier climates may be unable to handle peak Houston rainfall rates, causing water to back up against the fascia. Underlayment condition matters more here than in drier cities because it is regularly called on to prevent the water that shingles alone cannot stop. When assessing a Houston-area roof, Home Team evaluates drainage performance and waterproofing conditions based on the property's accessible and visible systems.

items.q: My Houston home has an older flat or low-slope section — does Home Team service those?
items.a: Houston's architectural diversity includes a significant number of homes with flat or low-slope roof sections — particularly on covered patios, garage extensions, and mid-century homes. These sections require different materials and installation techniques than pitched asphalt shingle roofing. Contact Home Team to discuss your specific situation; our team can assess the condition of low-slope areas and provide options appropriate for those roof types.

items.q: When is the right time to replace a roof in Houston versus repair it?
items.a: In Houston's climate, the calculus between repair and replacement tips toward replacement earlier than in milder areas. A roof approaching 15–20 years old on standard asphalt shingles has been through multiple hurricane seasons, tens of thousands of UV hours, and significant cumulative rainfall. If a roof in this age range shows widespread granule loss, multiple areas of damage, or has required repeated repairs, replacement usually delivers better long-term value than continued patch work. Home Team provides an honest assessment rather than defaulting to either option — we show you the actual condition and let you decide with full information.

items.q: What does a free roof inspection include?
items.a: Every property is different, so Home Team Roofing tailors each roof inspection to the property's roofing system, visible conditions, and specific concerns. Depending on the property, the inspection may include evaluating accessible shingles or roofing materials, flashing, drainage areas, visible storm damage, and other relevant roofing components. Additional areas are assessed when appropriate and accessible. After the inspection, our team explains its findings and discusses recommended repair or replacement options.

items.q: Is financing available for Houston roofing projects?
items.a: Yes. Home Team offers flexible financing options to help Greater Houston homeowners manage the cost of a roofing project without delay. Ask about available payment plans during your free inspection or visit the financing page for more information.

topic1.heading: Intense Heat and UV Exposure
topic1.body: Houston-area summers push roof surface temperatures well above the ambient air temperature. Over time, heat and UV radiation break down shingle granules, accelerate asphalt oxidation, and shorten the functional life of an improperly ventilated roof. Quality attic ventilation is not optional in this climate — it is a performance requirement.

topic2.heading: Hurricane and Storm Exposure
topic2.body: Greater Houston sits in one of the most hurricane-active corridors in the United States. Even storms that make landfall away from the city can deliver sustained winds that stress or damage shingles, flashing, and ridge caps. Between hurricane seasons, frequent severe thunderstorms produce localized hail and high-wind events that can cause damage not visible from the ground. If your roof sustained storm damage, Home Team can help you understand your repair and replacement options — including navigating the process when an insurance claim is involved. Insurance coverage decisions are made by your carrier; our role is to help you understand what your roof actually needs.

topic3.heading: High Annual Rainfall
topic3.body: Houston receives substantial annual rainfall, making roof drainage and water resistance important considerations for local property owners. Frequent heavy rain events put every flashing seal, penetration, and drainage system on a residential roof under repeated stress. Gutters and downspouts sized for drier climates may be insufficient for peak Houston rainfall rates. When assessing a Houston-area roof, Home Team evaluates drainage performance and waterproofing conditions based on the property's accessible and visible systems.

topic4.heading: Impact-Resistant Shingles for Houston Homes
topic4.body: Impact-resistant shingles — rated Class 3 or Class 4 under the UL 2218 test standard — offer significantly better durability against hail than standard asphalt shingles. Class 4 shingles have demonstrated resistance to impacts that would penetrate or crack standard materials, and they may qualify for homeowner insurance discounts in Texas. In a market where hail events and high-wind storms recur regularly, upgrading to impact-resistant materials at replacement time is a cost-effective long-term decision.
